prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: refined game art and original unobtrusive HUD concept for Last Chance Resort.
Input image 1: EDIT TARGET, the approved futuristic enclosed arena with realistic rendered art and an oversized generic HUD.
Primary request: substantially refine the gift-delivery drones and robot hazards, and redesign the interface to be much LESS NOTICEABLE and more ORIGINAL. Completely remove the keyboard hints along the bottom. Preserve the approved realistic stylized rendered art, dimensional materials, warm amber/cyan lighting and fixed side-view 2D gameplay. The result is a polished, plausible game screenshot, not a poster or design board.

Keep unchanged: overall 16:10 landscape framing, enclosed glass-and-metal dome, outdoor palms visible through glass, straight playable floor, both original adult players with their same believable anatomy, outfits and airborne poses, ball and thin edge-on central net. Preserve the original soft background hierarchy and lighting. Keep the gameplay plane and readable open air between characters.

Art refinement:
- Replace the two generic quadcopters with a distinctive coordinated family of luxury-resort COURIER DRONES. Same hover positions and approximately same size. Elegant flattened ivory hull shaped like a small travel case, champagne-metal spine and graphite undershell, four unmistakable compact propeller assemblies with slim protective guard arcs, translucent rotor blur. A small horizontal cyan/orange status slit rather than a large cartoon eye; small angled stabilizer fins and discreet hinged cargo arms. A tiny understated luggage-tag pictogram gives them the character of hospitality equipment. Left courier teal accents, right courier muted coral accents. Clearly show four rotors, no insect wings.
- Upgrade gift cargo: premium small cream hard-shell parcel cases with a restrained teal/coral ribbon band, a readable bow, a small hanging travel-tag and metal corner clips. Use a compact balanced gripper attachment, no dangling tangled cables. Gifts fully distinct beneath drone hulls. Refined readable silhouettes, not detailed miniature clutter.
- Redesign the SPRING hazard at lower left as an absurd resort fitness assistant: compact sculpted ivory-and-burnt-orange base, two little stabilizing feet, one oversized exposed brushed-steel coil, a broad softly padded circular cap resembling a small fitness rebound platform, rubber shock stops and a very small amber status slit. The spring's mechanical compression and bend must read clearly. Preserve its approximate placement and the relationship to the tumbling man. Show credible contact shadow and slight floor reflection, restrained curved motion trace only.
- Redesign the EXPRESS PORTER at lower right as an original automated BELLHOP rather than a generic cute robot: a low stable graphite wheel chassis with two readable rubber wheels and champagne hubs, a slim ivory concierge body, small horizontal amber face/status slit, a low swept-back luggage rail inspired by a hotel luggage trolley, two neatly stacked cream and muted coral cases secured with a dark strap. A little brass bell-like dome on top of the body hints at hotel service. Quiet ergonomic curves, lightly worn surfaces and rubber bumpers. Keep it compact, clearly a ground hazard speeding left. Two short motion streaks, no smoke or explosions.
- Refine foreground material craftsmanship: subtle court seams, realistic rubber and brushed metal, wall service buttons inset in small sculpted sockets with thin illumination rings. Keep scenery subdued and objects readable. Do not increase background clutter or turn everything into glowing sci-fi machinery.

NEW UI DESIGN: think understated arena instrumentation plus premium hotel luggage tags, NOT generic game cards. Remove ALL current large score boxes, glowing capsule toolbar, broad power bars, oversized bordered buttons and the ENTIRE bottom keyboard-hint row. Restore continuous original dark textured foreground where hints were.
- Small score readouts are lightly integrated into upper-left and upper-right arena support beams, no floating rectangular card background. At x9% y5%-12% place exact small label "YOU" above a restrained pale cyan score "4", roughly 4% of frame height, with three tiny amber/cyan touch dots beneath (two filled, one dim). At x89% y5%-12% exact small label "CPU" above pale coral score "3", with three tiny touch dots (one filled, two dim). A fine short bracket line connects each readout visually to the structural support. Low-bloom etched illuminated-display look, easy to read but much quieter than the scene objects.
- At top center, one NARROW asymmetric ticket-like status strip within x39%-61%, y3%-8%, no thick full border and almost transparent graphite fill: tiny magnet pictogram, exact text "NEXT: MAGNET", a delicate perforation line, tiny exact text "TO 10". Give it a clipped corner and one tiny amber registration notch. This subtle resort service-ticket motif is the ORIGINAL visual identity of the HUD.
- Directly below the strip at y9% place THREE tiny icon-only controls (pause, sound, fullscreen), approximately 1.5% frame height each, widely spaced and low-contrast off-white. No boxed buttons or bright outlines.
- Under the left score use only a tiny spring glyph with "8s"; under the right score use a tiny lightning glyph with "18s". Each paired with a slim incomplete arc showing remaining duration, no long bar, no descriptive panel. Delicate practical vector-like UI marks harmonized with the arena architecture. Do not add titles, extra labels, health bars, currencies or menus.
- Keep all interface in the top 16% of image, comfortably clear of drone rotor silhouettes. No overlays along the bottom, no keycaps, no control instructions, no extra labels attached to players or the court.
- UI must occupy much less visual area than in the reference, maintaining contrast for legibility but restrained colour intensity. Foreground players, drones and hazards remain the focus.

Text in English, accurately rendered, only the exact short strings specified. Maintain the reference's sophisticated rendering and anatomy. Avoid cartoon/vector-style scene redraw, thick outlines, arbitrary new characters, weapons, tactical military drones, cyberpunk clutter, gigantic robot eyes, large glowing UI panels, particle fog, overexposure, extra balls, extra nets, collage, explanatory callouts or watermarks.
